holidays.name: International Moment of Frustration Scream Day
holidays.description: Today is officially a day to let it all out. At noon Universal Time, people step outside and scream at the top of their lungs for 30 seconds. It's a quick and noisy way to get rid of stress. Neighbors may be confused, but you'll feel lighter.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance. It began as a tongue-in-cheek call for people everywhere to scream away their frustrations together at the same moment.
holidays.funFact: Noon Universal Time is early morning in the Americas. In Pacific time it falls around 5 a.m., so many participants just scream into a pillow or sleep through it and try again later.

holidays.name: National Gumbo Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates gumbo, the rich and hearty stew that is Louisiana's official state cuisine. It starts with a strongly flavored stock and is loaded with meat or shellfish. It's built on the 'Holy Trinity' of celery, bell peppers and onions. Grab a bowl and a spoon, and put the rice on.
holidays.origin: Gumbo grew out of Louisiana's blend of West African, French, Spanish and Native American cooking traditions. The day is an unofficial food observance that honors the dish.
holidays.funFact: Many gumbo recipes start with a roux, a mix of flour and fat stirred patiently until it darkens. Cooks sometimes say a good roux can't be rushed, and a burnt one means starting over.

holidays.name: Freethought Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates independent thinking, skepticism and reasoning over blind belief. It is sometimes called Freethought 'Coming Out' Day. It invites people to question ideas, follow the evidence and talk openly about their views.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance, commonly marked on October 12 by freethinkers and skeptic communities.
holidays.funFact: The calendar's neighbors fit the theme: International Skeptics Day follows right on October 13.
